The combination of lower motor neuron involvement in one leg with paresis and fasciculations combined with muscular rigidity and superimposed spasms add to the clinical heterogeneity of SPS-related disorders. ... The prominent lower motor neuron signs and the relentless and progressive course that led to death after 18 months is not typical for SPS, but rather points to a diagnosis of PER. ... The patient also suffered typical symptoms of SPS with tonically maintained rigidity and muscle cramps, supporting the relevance of the concept “SPS plus” syndromes [16].
